items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions James P. Johnson in the context of stride piano style; INTERVIEWEE does not mention James P. Johnson directly nor describe a personal interaction.

ctx.x: If you heard the piano, he was tinkling in there, and the bass horn was just going boom-te-boom, and those things. But, still, they swung in those days.

They swung, all right. I mean, though, the thing is that until Earl came along with that style of -- that stride style of Fats and James P. Johnson was fine in the solo, but it didn't really go with the bass drums, did it?
No. And you have to say that Earl definitely was the father of making a solo pianist being heard and appreciated in a big band.
